name: Dysautonomia Awareness Month launch
notes: First five slideshows: relatability, proof, a save-worthy listicle, awareness month, and the giveaway.

creatives.name: POV: you stood up
creatives.title: My heart hit 140 making coffee ☕
creatives.goal: Widest-net relatability. No selling until the last slide.
creatives.caption: POV: your heart rate when you stand up. If this is you, you're not imagining it 🩵 #pots #dysautonomia #longcovid #chronicillness #spoonie

text: POV: you got up to make coffee & your HR hit *140.*

img.shows: A white drip coffee maker against a dark wall.
img.frame: Machine in the lower half; the hook sits in the dark space above it under a light wash.
img.credit: Photo by Ronan Furuta on Unsplash (unsplash.com/photos/white-and-black-coffeemaker-AjcABUQ7WuA)

text: Everyone said it was anxiety.
Your smartwatch said *otherwise.*

img.shows: The Autonomic watch app's live heart-rate monitor at 143 BPM, Δ +36, composited onto a wrist.
img.frame: Watch in the top third, clear of the copy.
img.credit: Wrist photo by Anastasiya Badun on Unsplash (unsplash.com/photos/a-person-holding-an-apple-watch-in-their-hand-EK6J3PLsndY); screen is the Autonomic watch app

text: If your body does this, you're not imagining it.
And you're *not alone.*

img.shows: A woman at a kitchen table at night, head resting on her hand, eyes half closed, a mug in front of her.
img.frame: Wide photo cropped to her and the mug; face in the upper third, the copy over the darkened lower half.

text: I know it's real because I can *see it.*
Free app in bio if you want to *track yours.* 🩵

img.shows: Progress, POTS section: stand tests over 12 weeks. Latest sustained rise 51 bpm (red), standing peak +74 on a 69 baseline (about 143 bpm), 12 of 12 over the POTS threshold, both lines climbing.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot; the falling chart sits in the top two thirds.

music.mood: Soft lo-fi with a wry edge
music.notes: Relatable, not sad. A mellow lo-fi beat or a deadpan trending POV sound carries the hook; it should feel like a shrug at slide 1 and turn tender by slide 3. Keep it low under the text so the words land.

creatives.name: My data saw it coming
creatives.title: My watch saw my crash coming 3 days early
creatives.caption: My HRV saw the crash coming 3 days before I did. Pacing changed everything. #mecfs #longcovid #pacing #hrv #chronicfatigue

text: My watch knew I was going to crash *3 days* before I did.

img.shows: You looking wiped out in a dim bedroom.
img.frame: Face in the upper third; the hook sits across the middle under a dark wash. Low light is fine, it is the mood.

text: My HRV dropped 3 days straight.
I felt fine. *The data didn't agree.*

img.shows: Your real HRV trend dropping over several days.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot. Put the falling chart in the top two thirds of the screen.

text: By the time I felt it, *I'd already been warned.*

img.shows: Progress or Insights showing the crash day.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot, crash day visible in the top two thirds.

text: Now I pace *before* the crash, not after.
Free app I built, link in bio.

img.shows: The Journal home: Today row, the Outlook card with the score (96), pacing strip and key figures, giveaway card collapsed.
img.frame: Full-height screenshot from the top; move or shrink the phone to show more of it.

music.notes: A slow-building ambient pulse, almost a heartbeat, so the three days of falling HRV feel like a countdown. No big drop. Let it open up into something warmer on the last slide, where you pace before the crash.

creatives.title: 5 POTS signs my doctors missed for years
creatives.caption: Save this for your next appointment 🩵 5 signs of POTS that took years to get taken seriously. #pots #potsawareness #dysautonomia #chronicillness

text: 5 signs you might have *POTS*
(that doctors kept missing for me)

img.shows: A minimal, clean background with lots of negative space.
img.frame: Soft texture or gradient with no focal subject. It is fully darkened under the headline.
img.credit: Photo by Luke Chesser on Unsplash (unsplash.com/photos/light-blue-to-dark-blue-gradient-3rWagdKBF7U)

text: 1. Heart races when you stand
2. Dizzy or lightheaded upright
3. Wiped out after small tasks
4. Brain fog
5. Everything's worse in heat

img.shows: A calm, simple background: linen, paper, soft sky.
img.frame: Darkened ~85% under the list, so texture matters more than subject.
img.credit: Photo by Heather Green on Unsplash (unsplash.com/photos/a-light-blue-fabric-textured-with-a-diagonal-pattern-VYeNQq9SnnE)

slides.fine: Not medical advice. Ask your doctor about a stand test.

text: I tracked all of it to *show my doctor.*
Free app in bio to track yours. 🩵

img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot with logged symptoms near the top.

music.notes: Light acoustic or a clean upbeat lo-fi that keeps people swiping through the list without competing with it. Steady from start to finish, no drops or vocals over the list slides. Saves come from re-reading, so it should loop well.

creatives.name: They said it was in my head
creatives.title: They said it was all in my head
creatives.caption: Not just a feeling. It's data I can track and share. October is Dysautonomia Awareness Month 🩵 #dysautonomiaawareness #longcovid #pots #invisibleillness

text: People told me my long COVID was *‘in my head.’*

img.shows: An honest window-light portrait of you.
img.frame: Face in the upper third, looking at the camera or out the window. The hook covers the middle under a dark wash.

text: So I recorded what my heart *actually does* when I stand up.

img.shows: HRV / heart rate during a standing test.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot; the standing jump in heart rate should be in the top two thirds.

text: Now it's not just a feeling. *It's data I can track and share.*

img.shows: Two hands passing a small black paper heart, plain light background.
img.frame: Backdrop extended below the photo so the heart sits in the upper half, above the line.

text: Track yours. *See what helps or hurts your numbers.*
Watch your autonomic system recover!
Free app for iOS and Android, link in my bio.

img.shows: The Journal home, not scrolled: Today row, the Outlook card with the Autonomic score, pacing strip and key figures.

music.notes: Sparse piano under the first slide, building with strings through the standing test, peaking on "You can't fake a heart rate", then resolving hopeful for the awareness-month close. Instrumental only, so your words stay the voice.

creatives.name: The giveaway
creatives.title: I'm giving away an Apple Watch 🩵
creatives.caption: Giving away an Apple Watch to the POTS & long COVID community this Dysautonomia Awareness Month 🩵 How to enter: download Autonomic (free on iOS & Android, link in bio), sign up on the giveaway card in the Journal, and take an HRV reading each morning (your phone's camera works, no special equipment needed). One entry per day, up to 10 entries, Oct 1 to Oct 31. US residents 18+, no purchase necessary. Your health data stays on your phone. Not affiliated with TikTok or Apple. #giveaway #pots #longcovid #dysautonomia
